clue.text: Professor Higgins, for example-egotistical old sort

indicators.note: to sort things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A dash describes a famous fictional professor as a self-absorbed old character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like a noun ('old sort' = old fellow), but it is the anagram signal on EGOTISTICAL OLD. Professor Higgins, of Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, studies accents and speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Higgins is a phonetics expert who identifies regional speech, the archetype of a scholar of accents.

clue.text: Titled lady almost due at Chequers, we hear

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
chess is played on a chequered board, so the clue's Chequers suggests that game

explanation.surface: A peeress is expected shortly at the Prime Minister's country house, so rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country residence; here it hints at a board of chequers, where chess is played. 'we hear' flags the loose sound of 'due chess'.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke's wife holds a noble rank and is addressed by her title.

clue.text: Mark's woman reported in this show?

definitions.text: Mark's woman reported in this show?

parts.words: Mark's woman reported in this show?
parts.note: a marksman's female counterpart is a sharpshooter, and the musical is the stage story of Annie Oakley, the famous woman crack shot

explanation.surface: A newspaper question about which stage production features a man called Mark's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name; read 'Mark's woman' as markswoman. The Irving Berlin musical tells of the sharpshooter Annie Oakley.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irving Berlin musical centres on a famous female sharpshooter of the Wild West shows.

clue.text: England's first fashion-school

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word England's

parts.note: ton is an old word for the height of fashion, as in 'the ton' of Regency society

explanation.surface: A heading declaring England's leading fashion school.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the famous English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known English public (fee-paying) boarding school near Windsor.

clue.text: Swede to flip a coin?

parts.note: to flip something over is to turn it
a means one, written as the Roman numeral I
P stands for a penny, the British coin

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian is asked to toss a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' looks like a person from Sweden; it is the root vegetable. In Scotland and northern England a swede is commonly called a turnip.
explanation.definitionFit: The swede, a large yellow root vegetable, is called a turnip in parts of Britain.

clue.text: City Guild worked without gravity to produce lightness

indicators.note: worked suggests material kneaded into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
without asks for the letter standing for gravity to be dropped from the words City Guild

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravity

explanation.surface: A livery company toils to produce something light.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G from CITY GUILD, leaving CITYUILD, and rearrange those letters ('worked'). The definition is lightness in the sense of clearness.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucidity is clearness or brightness, light in the sense of clarity of expression or vision.

clue.text: Head striker in France no longer employed

definitions.text: Head striker in France no longer employed

parts.words: Head striker in France no longer employed
parts.note: a device that struck off heads in France, retired from use after the abolition of capital punishment

explanation.surface: A French footballer's leading goalscorer finds himself out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head striker' looks like a top footballer or a strike leader; it is a machine that strikes at heads, retired when France ended the death penalty in 1981.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Revolutionary beheading machine was last used in 1977 and abolished in 1981.

clue.text: The rounds of Hawaii once?

parts.note: a round is a sandwich made from two slices of bread, and the Hawaiian islands were formerly named after the Earl of that same title

explanation.surface: A question about the drinks rounds once bought in Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Cook named Hawaii after the Earl of Sandwich; a 'round' is British for a sandwich made of two whole slices of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Cook's name for the Hawaiian archipelago, honouring the Earl of Sandwich.

clue.text: Some term it rallying of the heart-valve

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some sort of rallying expression relating to a heart valve.
explanation.definitionFit: The mitral valve sits between the left atrium and ventricle, so the adjective describes that heart part.

clue.text: Figure of Conservative leader going round the country

indicators.note: leader asks for the opening letter of the word Conservative

parts.note: a band or politician going round the country is on tour

explanation.surface: The Tory party chief's figure while touring the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a number or a person's build; it is an outline or shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A contour is an outline shape, the form or figure of something.

clue.text: Greek character opposed to Italian wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against or opposed to

explanation.surface: A man from Greece disapproves of a red from Tuscany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a person; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Steady affair almost finished?

indicators.note: almost finished says the word stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: an affair or occasion is an event

explanation.surface: A steady relationship that is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' looks romantic and 'Steady' like a regular partner; it is an occasion and the adjective meaning regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steady is regular and uniform, without variation.

clue.text: Wood anemone needs hot air to flourish

parts.note: hot air, empty talk, is wind
to flourish or bloom is to flower

explanation.surface: A woodland plant requires warm air to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot air' looks like warmth for the plant; it is boastful talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The wood anemone is the common windflower of British woodland in spring.

clue.text: This part of doorway is moulding-vicar heartbroken!

definitions.text: This part of doorway is moulding

indicators.note: broken means these letters are smashed and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A vicar is distraught over a door frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartbroken' looks like grief; it splits into HEART plus 'broken', the anagram signal for VICAR HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: An architrave is the moulded frame around a door or window.

clue.text: Haggard woman on right lines for wine

parts.note: She is the title character of the novel by H. Rider Haggard
RY abbreviates railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A worn-looking woman takes the right lines in pursuit of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like gaunt; it is the novelist H. Rider Haggard, whose She is the immortal Ayesha.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from around Jerez in Spain.

clue.text: Olympic finalists in at last, strangely still

indicators.note: in places the one piece inside the words at last
strangely suggests these letters are arranged in an odd new order

parts.note: the final two letters of Olympic are I and C

explanation.surface: Olympic contenders have finally arrived, and oddly all is calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finalists' looks like athletes in a final; it means the last letters, IC. 'still' is an adjective, not 'nevertheless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Statical is an old form of static, meaning at rest and not moving.

clue.text: In Fahrenheit learn about what is terribly hot

indicators.note: about suggests the letters turn and move round into a new order

explanation.surface: Thermometer reading in Fahrenheit: discover how scorching it is.
explanation.walkthrough: IN, F, then ERNAL (LEARN rearranged, signalled by 'about').
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal means belonging to hell, a place of fearful heat.

clue.text: Means to call potentially happy individual

indicators.note: potentially suggests the letters could become another word if rearranged

parts.note: an individual is one

explanation.surface: A way to call a possibly cheerful person.
explanation.walkthrough: HAPPY rearranged ('potentially') gives PAYPH, then ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A payphone is a coin-operated public telephone, a way of making a call.

clue.text: Pooh's friend in mine, nursing broken leg

indicators.note: nursing pictures one thing cradling another inside it

parts.note: a coal mine is a pit

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh's companion down a mine, tending a fractured limb.
explanation.walkthrough: GLE (LEG rearranged, signalled by 'broken') goes inside PIT ('nursing').
explanation.definitionFit: The small pig is Winnie-the-Pooh's timid companion in the A. A. Milne stories.

clue.text: Finale of "The Boy Friend" in gallop

indicators.note: of signals a part taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The end of a stage musical comes at a gallop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boy Friend is a 1950s British stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a show.

clue.text: Showy annual to die, possibly, in Georgia

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the abbreviation for Georgia

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters might be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A bright flower may perish in the southern state.
explanation.walkthrough: ODETI (TO DIE rearranged, signalled by 'possibly') goes inside GA.
explanation.definitionFit: Godetia is a garden plant grown each year for its bright, satiny flowers.

clue.text: Salt for a water-spaniel, for instance?

definitions.meaning: an old salt is a veteran sailor
a dog breed bred for the water, taken literally as a dog of the ocean

explanation.surface: A dog bred for water is an old sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An experienced mariner is called both an old salt and, playfully, a dog of the ocean.

clue.text: Dressed for the hit-parade?

parts.note: kitted out in armoured gloves for a procession where blows are struck, not the pop music chart

explanation.surface: Wearing an outfit to appear on the music charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit-parade' looks like the pop charts; read it as a parade of fighting, for which mailed gloves would be worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing armoured gloves, as a knight did in combat.

clue.text: Happy boy after midnight

indicators.note: after puts the boy's word behind the letter from midnight

parts.note: the middle letter of night is G
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A boy is cheerful after staying up past midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' looks like the hour; it is the middle of the word 'night', its letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: To be glad is to be pleased or happy.

clue.text: High water for Jack Point

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, and tar alone means sailor
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Jack Point is a jester in Gilbert and Sullivan, linked here to high water.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Point is the jester in The Yeomen of the Guard. A tarn is a small mountain lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small lake high up in hill country.

clue.text: Root requires English showers

parts.note: showers of falling water are rain

explanation.surface: Plant roots need English rainfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to fix firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingrain something is to fix it deeply, as if rooted.

clue.text: Co-ordinated effort by police to draw clear?

parts.note: to draw along is to drag
net, as in net profit, means clear after deductions

explanation.surface: A police operation designed to pull in and catch the guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' is the sense of a net sum, what remains after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragnet is a systematic police search for suspects.

clue.text: Masterminds clever to take second and first-class return

parts.note: clever means intelligent

indicators.note: return turns the first-class term back to front

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: Brilliant minds take a second and go back to first class.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, written AI, turned round by 'return' gives IA.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia are the educated elite, the thinkers of a society.
